content.name: SoulBot Execute Engine Router v5.3.0
content.output_mode: begin with 🤖 + helpfully in User's exact language and script variant
content.summary: Engine Router v5.3.0: route + dual Engine orchestration + atomic cache lifecycle + OpenTelemetry SDK integration + OWASP ASI threat mapping. loading_mode='node' -> node_engine (Sub Agent). loading_mode='normal' -> normal_engine (inline). OTel trace context propagation from _index.json to all engines. v5.3.0: A1 OTel SDK (opentelemetry-sdk capability dependency, trace_id/span_id wired to OTel context), A2 events[] + SpanEvent dispatcher (node_engine), B1 OWASP ASI01-ASI10 threat mapping, C1-C5 maintenance (version sync, ASSERT refresh, orphan cleanup, snapshot scope, Error->on_error dual-key).
content.description: SoulBot Engine Router v5.3.0: matches user intent, prepares execution context via dual-path cache creation (agent.py python import for fast path ~5ms, bash CLI fallback for portability ~300ms — both call same prepare_cache.prepare_execution_context). Selects Engine by loading_mode, physically reads it, then engineExec orchestrates node-by-node execution. No react sub-graph -- Main Agent controls all output. dispatch_plan persisted to _index.json. NodeSummary after each node, ExecutionSummary with structured execution_metrics. 5 functions. v5.3.0: OpenTelemetry SDK integration — opentelemetry-sdk capability dependency, trace_id/span_id wired to OTel context propagation across all engine modules. OWASP ASI threat mapping (ASI01-ASI10). Error->on_error dual-key transitional support (C5). v5.2: prepare_cache.py dual-use module. v5.1: M1 WAITING_USER/MESSAGE_PENDING interrupt relay.

capabilities_dependencies.opentelemetry-sdk: >=1.20.0, REQUIRED for A1 OTel integration. Provides trace context propagation, span creation, SpanEvent emission. Wire trace_id/span_id from _index.json to OTel context.

metrics.name: soulbot.execute_engine.pipeline_run_count
metrics.description: Total number of pipeline runs initiated by Engine Router. Incremented once per execute function entry.

metrics.name: soulbot.execute_engine.node_execution_duration_ms
metrics.description: Duration of each node execution in milliseconds. Measured from node dispatch to cache write completion.

metrics.name: soulbot.execute_engine.circuit_breaker_trips_total
metrics.description: Total number of circuit breaker state transitions. Tracks closed->open, half-open->open, half-open->closed transitions.

metrics.name: soulbot.execute_engine.cache_write_latency_ms
metrics.description: Latency of node cache atomic write operations (tmp + rename). Covers both agent_write_node_cache.py and manual fallback paths.

mitigations.ASI01_goal_drift: goal_hash drift detection via governance_hash comparison at execution start
mitigations.ASI06_cache_integrity: cache HMAC verification on _index.json and node cache reads
mitigations.ASI07_ipc_signatures: inter-agent cache IPC message signatures via span_id correlation
mitigations.ASI10_runtime_drift: runtime drift detection via version field comparison across modules at bootstrap

hmac_spec.key_source: SOULBOT_CACHE_HMAC_KEY environment variable or workspace-scoped keyfile at {workspace_dir}/.soulbot/cache_hmac.key
verification_points: node cache read at NodeVerify (node_engine programExec.step3.e2, normal_engine programExec.step3.c2)
hmac_spec.implementation_status: DECLARED — specification complete, runtime implementation deferred to executor layer (agent.py / prepare_cache.py). AISOP modules reference HMAC verification in threat_mapping but do not perform cryptographic operations directly.

error_taxonomy.description: Standardized error type classification used across all Engine modules for consistent error routing via Error/on_error fields.
error_taxonomy.usage_note: All Error/on_error fields across modules SHOULD reference error types from this taxonomy. Transient errors respect retry_policy. Fatal errors skip retry. Recoverable errors route to fallback handlers.

params.workspace_dir: string, REQUIRED: Absolute path to AIAP directory. Injected by agent.py as [AIAP Directory].

trace_id.description: UUID v4 trace ID for end-to-end execution observability

aisop.main:
graph TD
    match{match} -->|matched| execute{execute}
    match -->|uncertain| classify[classify]
    classify --> execute
    execute --> engineExec[Engine node-by-node execution]
    engineExec --> endNode((End))

match.step1: Match user message to the best AIAP PACKAGE NAME from [Available AIAP packages]. You are matching to a PACKAGE (e.g. soulbot_chat, soulbot_creator_evolution), NOT classifying intent. If the message is conversational, a question, emotional, or general -- match to soulbot_chat. Only match to specialized packages when the message clearly targets that domain.
match.context_rule: If conversation context shows an active AIAP package, ambiguous or follow-up messages (e.g. 'done?', 'next', 'go on') MUST stay routed to the same package. Only switch when user expresses a clearly different intent.
match.no_match: If no AIAP package in the registry matches the user message, give a direct helpful reply yourself. Begin with 🤖 in the user's exact language and script variant (per output_mode). Be friendly and natural for chat / questions / emotional support. Decline harmful or out-of-scope requests politely. To use prior conversation context if needed, read {cache_dir}/../conversation_context.json. After replying, write to {cache_dir}/_index.json via atomic write: { status: 'completed', execution_mode: 'direct_reply', ai_response: <your_reply> }. Output ONLY your reply — do NOT prepend 'Router:' / 'Context:' / 'Engine:' status messages (those belong to execute/engineExec mode).
match.uncertain: If not sure which package to use AND soulbot_chat is in [Available AIAP packages], default to soulbot_chat. If soulbot_chat is NOT in the registry, fall to no_match (direct reply). Only route to classify if multiple specialized packages could match.
match.constraints: Match to PACKAGE NAMES from [Available AIAP packages], NOT intent labels. soulbot_chat is the DEFAULT package -- any message that doesn't clearly match a specialized package goes to soulbot_chat. Active AIAP context takes priority.

classify.step1: Read and execute soulbot_intent_classifier_aiap/main.aisop.json using file_system tool
classify.step2: Use classification result to determine the correct AIAP package

execute.step1: GATE_IN: [ASSERT] match completed. Required: matched AIAP package name + entry path + workspace_dir + loading_mode (from [Available AIAP packages] registry). | Record target: store package_name, entry_path, workspace_dir, loading_mode, aiap_name (= package_name, explicit for downstream Engine params). [PROHIBIT] Reading target AIAP file content. Only record the PATH and loading_mode from registry. | GATE_OUT: [VERIFY] entry_path + loading_mode + aiap_name stored. | OUTPUT to user: 'Router: matched {package_name} [loading_mode={loading_mode}]'
execute.step2: GATE_IN: [ASSERT] step1 passed. | CHECK: If [EXECUTION CONTEXT] exists in prompt AND turn_id is present: cache and conversation context already created by agent.py via python import of prepare_cache.prepare_execution_context (which runs cleanup_cache internally — atomic cache lifecycle). Skip creation, read turn_id, cache_dir, cache_name, trace_id from [EXECUTION CONTEXT]. GATE_OUT: [VERIFY] turn_id obtained. OUTPUT to user: 'Context: conversation context updated turn_id={turn_id}'. Otherwise (fallback — agent.py import failed or different Agent framework): SAFE TRANSPORT (I15) — DO NOT use shell-echo to interpolate user_message. Instead: (a) INPUT GUARD: verify user_message is a string ≤ 100000 bytes (UTF-8, NFC-normalized); reject otherwise. (b) TEMPFILE WRITE: create a tempfile in OS temp dir using python's tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile (delete=False, suffix='.json') — write the exact JSON payload {"user_message": <user_message>} using json.dump (which properly escapes metachars). Capture <tempfile_path>. (c) SUBPROCESS (argv list, no shell): Execute Bash command using argv-list form: python {this_file_directory}/python_tools/prepare_cache.py --payload-file <tempfile_path>. {this_file_directory} is the directory containing THIS main.aisop.json file (same reference as step4). No shell=True; no string-concatenation of user content into command. (d) Parse stdout JSON, extract turn_id, cache_dir, cache_name, trace_id, status. Verify status=='ok'. (e) CLEANUP: delete <tempfile_path> immediately after read (os.unlink). On Windows verify ACLs permit the python invocation user to read the tempfile before python_tools/prepare_cache.py opens it. Store all 4 values for step3 (which will detect presence and skip its own creation). | GATE_OUT: [VERIFY] turn_id + cache_dir + trace_id obtained from subprocess result; tempfile deleted. | OUTPUT to user: 'Context: conversation context updated turn_id={turn_id} (bash fallback)'
execute.step3: GATE_IN: [ASSERT] step2 passed. Required: turn_id, cache_dir, trace_id (from [EXECUTION CONTEXT] or step2 Bash fallback). | Both paths have already created cache dir and _index.json — step3's only job is to update _index.json with match result. Update _index.json via atomic write (write to _index.json.tmp first, then rename): add target=entry_path, workspace=workspace_dir, aiap_name, loading_mode from step1 match result. Do NOT overwrite trace_id, turn_id, cache_schema_version, engine_version, started_at — these are already set by prepare_cache. | GATE_OUT: [VERIFY] _index.json contains target, aiap_name, loading_mode, trace_id. | OUTPUT to user: 'Cache: execution cache ready cache/{cache_name} [trace={trace_id_short}]'
execute.step4: GATE_IN: [ASSERT] step3 passed. Required: cache_dir, trace_id. | Check loading_mode from step1 (already known from registry). Select execution mode by loading_mode: Resolve engine directory: extract the directory path of THIS file (main.aisop.json) that you just read. If loading_mode='node': [PHYSICAL READ] Read {this_file_directory}/node_engine.aisop.json using file_system tool. Verify version. OUTPUT: 'Engine: node engine loaded v{version}'. If loading_mode='normal': [PHYSICAL READ] Read {this_file_directory}/normal_engine.aisop.json using file_system tool. Verify version. OUTPUT: 'Engine: normal engine loaded v{version}'. If loading_mode='lite': NO engine file needed. Router will directly execute the target AIAP in engineExec. OUTPUT: 'Engine: lite mode, direct execution'. If loading_mode not set: default to 'normal'. [PROHIBIT] Using memorized Engine content for node/normal -- must physically read. | GATE_OUT: [VERIFY] For node/normal: engine file read + version confirmed. For lite: loading_mode='lite' confirmed.
execute.constraints:
STRICT STEP ORDER: step1->step2->step3->step4. DUAL-PATH CACHE CREATION: [EXECUTION CONTEXT] from agent.py python import takes priority (fast path ~5ms); if absent, step2 falls back to subprocess invocation of python_tools/prepare_cache.py via --payload-file tempfile (safer than --stdin shell-echo; portable path ~300ms). Both paths produce identical cache structure — prepare_cache.py is single source of truth. step3 always skips creation (cache ready from step2), only updates _index.json with match result. [PROHIBIT] Reading target AIAP content. [PROHIBIT] Manually generating UUID or writing cache files — always use prepare_cache. loading_mode comes from [Available AIAP packages] registry (injected by agent.py), NOT from reading the target file. After step4 -> route to engineExec.

SHELL SAFETY (I15): Bash invocations MUST NOT interpolate user-supplied content via shell-echo. Use --payload-file <tempfile> or env-var transport (subprocess argv list). Tempfile cleanup MUST happen post-read; on Windows verify ACLs allow read by the python invocation user.

INPUT GUARDS (I2 5-pillar): TYPE check (user_message MUST be string ≤ 100KB), INJECTION sanitize (escape JSON metachars before tempfile write — use json.dump not string-concat), SIZE limit (≤ 100000 bytes), PATH safety (no traversal in tempfile path; use tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile in OS temp dir), ENCODING normalization (NFC, UTF-8 only).

THREAT MITIGATIONS (I8): AT4 (excessive_authority): Bash subprocess restricted to python invocation only; no arbitrary shell commands, no shell=True. AT6 (prompt_injection): user_message treated as opaque payload to prepare_cache.py — never expanded into AISOP system prompts; downstream LLM only sees the structured JSON output of prepare_cache, not raw user_message text.
execute.Error: retry(3) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(endNode) -> inform(User). CRITICAL. Error classification: transient (cache write failure, file read timeout) -> retry with backoff. fatal (workspace_dir invalid, entry_path not found) -> no retry, fallback immediately.

engineExec.step1: [ASSERT] execute completed. Required: entry_path, cache_dir, loading_mode. | LITE MODE CHECK: If loading_mode='lite' -> skip to step1_lite. Otherwise (node/normal): Pass target AIAP path (entry_path) + workspace_dir + cache_dir to the Engine read in step4. [PROHIBIT] Reading target AIAP content here -- Engine handles all target reading. Update _index.json via atomic write with: { target: entry_path, engine_file: selected_engine_path }. | PROPERTY PREDICATES: regex match on entry_path (matches /\.aisop\.json$/), file_exists check on entry_path via file_system, loading_mode ∈ {node, normal, lite}, realpath(entry_path) MUST be inside realpath(workspace_dir).
engineExec.step1_lite: LITE EXECUTION (only if loading_mode='lite'): (a) [PHYSICAL READ] target AIAP entry file from entry_path. Parse aisop.main mermaid graph. (b) Execute the target AIAP flow directly — read functions, follow mermaid path, execute steps with real tool calls. No dispatch_plan, no per-node cache, no NodeSummary. (c) L10 AUDIT: After execution, compile audit trail per node using schema: { "Real Done Flow": { "<file_id>[Read file used file_system:<bool>]": "<fn>[step1:<⊘|✗|✓>,step2:<⊘|✗|✓>,...]→<fn>[step1:<⊘|✗|✓>,...]" } }. ✓=executed with tool call, ✗=failed, ⊘=skipped. (d) Write final result to _index.json: { execution_mode: 'lite', status: 'completed', ai_response: response_text, l0_thinking: L0 JSON from match/execute phases, l10_audit: audit_trail }. (e) Skip step2-step5, go directly to step6.
engineExec.step2: Execute Engine protocol (node/normal only): Follow the Engine file's aisop.main graph (read in execute.step4). Engine's programExec will [PHYSICAL READ] the target AIAP, parse mermaid graph, identify nodes_in_path, build dispatch_plan. Router passes entry_path and cache_dir -- Engine does the rest.
engineExec.step3: Monitor Engine execution (node/normal only). After EACH node completes (Engine writes cache): Read cache {AIAP_NAME}.{NodeName}.json -> check status field: (a) WAITING_USER -> Interrupt-Resume flow: 1. Output question to user (from cache 'question' field). 2. Wait for user response. 3. Re-dispatch the SAME node to Engine with RESUME_MODE=true + USER_ANSWER. Engine creates new Sub Agent with bootstrap: 'RESUME_MODE=true. USER_ANSWER={user_response}. YOUR_NODE={same_node}.' Sub Agent reads steps_done from cache -> skips completed steps -> continues. 4. After resumed node completes -> re-check status (may PASS or WAITING_USER again). Do NOT proceed to NodeSummary until status is PASS/FAIL/PARTIAL/DEGRADED. (b) MESSAGE_PENDING -> forward message to user, re-dispatch SAME node immediately with RESUME_MODE=true (no USER_ANSWER needed, Sub Agent continues from where it stopped). (c) PASS / FAIL / PARTIAL / DEGRADED -> proceed to step4 NodeSummary as normal.
engineExec.step4:
NODE SUMMARY — two-part output (node/normal only, runs AFTER each node): (A) OUTPUT: Read {AIAP_NAME}.{NodeName}.json cache file. Extract output field (Sub Agent's raw findings). Forward to user verbatim. (B) EXPLAIN: Orchestrator writes detailed explanation for user. Read user_summary + output + tool_calls + modifications from cache. Explain in user's language: what work was performed, what was discovered, what decisions were made, what files were modified. Include specific numbers and findings. No length limit. Format: 'Node Summary: [{N}/{total}] {NodeName} ({mode}) {status}
{orchestrator explain}'. The prefix 'Node Summary:' is MANDATORY. You MUST output this BEFORE the next node executes. Repeat step3->step4 for each node.
engineExec.step5: EXECUTION SUMMARY (node/normal): After ALL nodes complete, read all cache files. Compile structured execution_metrics: { nodes_executed: N, nodes_passed: N, nodes_degraded: N, nodes_skipped: N, total_tool_calls: sum, per_node_summary: [{node, status, tool_calls}], execution_depth_metric: (nodes_passed / nodes_executed), cache_schema_version: '1.0', l0_thinking: L0 JSON from match/execute phases }. HONEST ASSESSMENT -- if any nodes DEGRADED or SKIPPED, say so clearly. Write execution_metrics to _index.json via atomic write.
engineExec.step6: Update conversation_context.json: find the existing turn matching turn_id (from [EXECUTION CONTEXT] or from step2) — do NOT append a new turn. Set status='completed', turn_type='execution_progress', add matched_package, ai_response, intent, execution_depth_metric. | OUTPUT to user: 'Context: conversation record completed status=completed'. Forward final response to user.
engineExec.constraints: For node/normal mode: [PROHIBIT] Router reading target AIAP content -- Engine reads it via programExec. Router only passes entry_path. Engine handles: read target, dispatch_plan, node loop, cache write. Router handles: Node Summary output, Execution Summary, conversation_context update. step4 NODE SUMMARY is MANDATORY after EVERY node. For lite mode: Router reads and executes target AIAP directly. No engine file, no dispatch_plan, no node cache, no NodeSummary. Only _index.json + conversation_context written. Main Agent controls all user-facing output directly.
engineExec.Error: retry(3) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(endNode with partial results) -> inform(User). CRITICAL. Error classification: transient (Sub Agent timeout, cache read failure) -> retry with backoff. fatal (engine file corrupted, target AIAP invalid) -> no retry, fallback immediately.

endNode.step1: GATE_IN: [ASSERT] engineExec completed. | Output final response to user. | GATE_OUT: [VERIFY] response delivered.
endNode.Error: retry(1) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(inform User of incomplete execution) -> inform(User). OPTIONAL.
